Subject: Order form question: emergency maint & credits

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending over the latest order form. Two quick items our ops/legal team flagged when reviewing the SLA:

1) Emergency maintenance carveouts — the current draft treats emergency maintenance as excluded from uptime calculations but doesn’t define the approval path or notification timeline. We need a clear process for declaring something an emergency maintenance event and a maximum retroactive window for such declarations.

2) Credit staircase — your order form lists service credits as a flat percentage per incident. For our internal governance we need a staircase model (tiered credits by cumulative downtime per month) with a maximum cap and an option to escalate to a financial remedy beyond credits if downtime crosses a threshold.

Can your team propose specific language (and proposed % bands + caps)? Also, what is Redwood's stance on a 30-minute response-time SLA for P1 incidents related to infrastructure (not application-level)?

Appreciate a quick turn — our procurement run is tight this quarter.

Best,
Liam
Operations Lead
Summit Analytics

Team and Priya —

I put together a targeted redline (attached: sla_redline_v3.pdf) and a plain-language summary below. I tried to balance Summit's ask with Redwood's operational realities. High-level recommendations:

1) Emergency Maintenance (EM) definition & process- Definition: "Emergency Maintenance" = unscheduled work required to mitigate an active security, safety, or platform-wide integrity incident.
- Declaration process: Incident Commander (Redwood) may declare EM; Redwood must notify the customer by email and an incident page within 30 minutes of declaration. Customer may dispute claim within 72 hours; disputed claims revert to standard maintenance rules absent joint agreement.
- Retroactive window: Redwood may assert EM status for work completed in the prior 24 hours if correlated to the same incident and documented in the incident log.

2) Staircase credit model (monthly cumulative downtime basis)- 0 to 30 minutes: 0% credit- >30 to 120 minutes: 5% credit- >120 to 240 minutes: 12% credit- >240 minutes: 25% credit- Monthly credit cap: 50% of monthly fees for impacted services- Trigger for financial remedy beyond credits: cumulative monthly downtime > 480 minutes (8 hours) — parties may escalate to a defined executive review with right to negotiate partial refund or termination for material breach.

3) P1 response times- Hosted: Acknowledgement within 60 minutes; initial triage/update within 4 hours.- Dedicated/Private with Enterprise Support Add-on: Acknowledgement within 30 minutes; triage within 1 hour.

4) Additional guardrails- Credit computation excludes scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours' notice) and EMs as defined above unless EM is caused by Redwood negligence proven post-incident.- Maintenance notification windows: scheduled maintenance requires 72 hours' notice; minor rolling maintenance (under 2 hours per region) allowed weekly with 48 hours' notice.

I included suggested exact redline text in the PDF. A couple of negotiation levers that might help close: raising the monthly cap to 60% for sensitive Fortune customers, or offering a 30-minute P1 for Hosted for an additional monthly fee.

Action items:
- Jasmine: send sla_redline_v3.pdf + one-page summary to Liam and Priya.
- Aditya: confirm operational feasibility of 24-hour retroactive EM declaration and logging practice.
- Lauren: confirm finance comfortable with 50% cap vs 60% concession.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
